title: Input- and Feature-Space Correction for Cross-Hospital IHC Grading
desc: Pathology foundation models (FMs) are trained predominantly on hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) images but are increasingly used as frozen feature extractors for immunohistochemistry (IHC), where cross-hospital differences can impair grading. However, systematic comparisons of correction methods for cross-hospital IHC grading remain limited. To address this gap, we benchmark label-free transformations applied to input images before frozen-FM encoding and to features after frozen-FM encoding using UNI and Virchow2, three IHC markers, and six directed cross-hospital transfers, yielding 12 settings. Among the evaluated input-space methods, our proposed method FIX achieved the largest macro-F1 improvement over no correction, outperforming well-known stain normalization techniques. Among feature-space methods, a simple feature-wise standardization achieved the best improvement over no correction, outperforming CORAL. Under patient-averaged tile-level evaluation, combining FIX with feature-wise standardization improved macro-F1 and quadratic weighted kappa (QWK) by 0.181 and 0.208, respectively, and reduced ordinal error by 0.209 relative to no correction. These results show that input- and feature-space transformations can provide complementary benefits for cross-hospital IHC grading with frozen pathology FMs.

title: Machine Learning in Hand Pathology Diagnosis: A Narrative Review of Current Insights.
desc: [Hand (New York, N.Y.)] Machine learning (ML), a subset of artificial intelligence (AI), is revolutionizing health care. Given the intricate anatomy and functional complexity of the hand, AI applications in hand pathology are gaining prominence, particularly in the diagnosis of fractures, nerve injuries, and musculoskeletal disorders. This review summarizes ML advancements in hand pathology diagnosis, enhancing clinical history analysis, examination findings interpretation, and imaging assessment. A systematic search of PubMed, Google Scholar, EMBASE, Cochrane CENTRAL, Scopus, and Web of Science from 1901 to March 2025 was conducted, focusing on ML applications in diagnosing hand fractures, tendon injuries, and nerve compressions. The inclusion criteria encompassed original research, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and observational studies that demonstrated the use of AI in diagnostic imaging, preoperative assessment, or postoperative management. Studies that did not involve AI-driven diagnostic applications or lacked sufficient methodological transparency were excluded. Machine learning models, particularly convolutional neural networks (CNNs), have demonstrated high diagnostic accuracy in detecting fractures. Studies have validated CNNs in the detection of distal radius and ulna fractures, outperforming trainees and urgent care physicians. In addition, AI has enhanced clinical examination by integrating wearable motion sensors for objective joint assessment. However, challenges such as external validation, interpretability, and integration into clinical workflows remain, limiting broader clinical adoption. Machine learning shows promise in hand pathology diagnosis, but widespread adoption requires improved external validation, standardized methods, and interdisciplinary collaboration. Future research should prioritize multicentric studies and explainable AI to enhance trust and integration.

title: Really Need Recursion? Revisiting One-pass Registration with Multi-level Multi-space Contextual Guidance
desc: Deformable image registration is a fundamental challenge in medical image analysis. Recent deep learning-based methods typically adopt either one-pass architectures that complete registration in a single network iteration, or recursive architectures that refine registration through multiple passes. While recursive methods often improve accuracy, they incur substantial computational overhead and slower inference speed. In this paper, we challenge the necessity of recursion for high-performance deformable registration and propose M2CG, a one-pass registration network with Multi-level Multi-space Contextual Guidance. It performs multi-step progressive pyramid registration within a single iteration, guided at each step by contextual cues from three levels (previous, current, and subsequent steps) and four spaces (image space, image feature space, segmentation space, and segmentation feature space). Our M2CG supports both unsupervised (without any labels) and semi-supervised (with segmentation labels for partial training data) registration, and has achieved state-of-the-art performance across two well-benchmarked inter-/intra-patient medical registration tasks with eight public datasets. Our findings suggest that the current reliance on recursion may stem from the absence of sufficient contextual cues that comprehensively characterize the remaining distance to the target alignment.

title: Beyond diagnostic accuracy: navigating the artificial intelligence data tsunami toward value-based implementation in gastroenterology.
desc: [Frontiers in artificial intelligence] Artificial intelligence (AI) in gastrointestinal (GI) endoscopy has evolved from its early application in simple edge detection to highly sophisticated technologies designed to improve detection of neoplastic and preneoplastic lesions and support clinical decision-making. However, this rapid technological evolution has generated a "data tsunami" or "datanami": an overwhelming and continuously expanding volume of information that, frequently, exceeds the ability of clinicians and patients to process, interpret, and apply it effectively. Substantial investments in AI have been driven by expectations of improved efficiency and reduced healthcare costs. Nevertheless, the metrics used to justify the adoption of AI-assisted diagnostic and therapeutic strategies remain inadequately standardized, leaving the true cost-effectiveness of these technologies uncertain. Current AI research in gastroenterology has primarily focused on improving diagnostic performance rather than evaluating long-term clinical outcomes or economic value. To address this limitation, investigators employ stochastic microsimulation models, which simulate individual patient trajectories and enable more robust assessments of cost-effectiveness. As the field progresses from AI to extended intelligence and, ultimately, intelligent assistance, the role of humans becomes increasingly central. Rather than replacing clinical judgment, AI should augment human expertise, with healthcare professionals serving as the critical link between technological innovation and meaningful clinical benefit. This review examines whether AI applications in GI diseases can be implemented cost-effectively in routine clinical practice for diagnosis and treatment. It further explores the indispensable human dimension of AI adoption, emphasizing accountability, reliability, ethical oversight, and responsible implementation as essential safeguards for current and future clinical applications.

title: Self-Reflective Chain-of-Thought (SRCoT): Evidence-Based Text Generation via a Closed-Loop Retrieve--Reflect--Revise Pipeline on Edge LLMs
desc: Large language models (LLMs) can generate fluent outputs that lack source support or conflict with local operational constraints. We introduce Self-Reflective Chain-of-Thought (SRCoT), a modular architecture that organizes generation as a closed Retrieve--Reflect--Revise loop. SRCoT separates environment state, persistent knowledge, accumulated experience, and short-term memory into provenance-labeled stores. BM25 retrieval supplies local context; subsequent passes expose intermediate drafts, missing-information markers, follow-up queries, and optional claim--evidence mappings. These artifacts inform retrieval, revision, clarification, or abstention decisions. We examine the architecture through qualitative, trace-based case studies in two fully synthetic settings: emergency medical services and Munich-Sim, an emergency-operations simulation. Local prototype runs on an Apple M4-family laptop with 128 GB memory illustrate source-labeled documentation, explicit gap marking, and structured dispatch-style outputs. The traces also reveal provenance-assignment errors, incomplete evidence coverage, and unsafe assumptions that remain possible despite prompting constraints. These cases demonstrate report-level inspectability and local execution, not comparative superiority, hallucination reduction, clinical validity, or operational safety. The architecture separates retrieval and control from the model interface, but behavior across different models remains to be evaluated. SRCoT is a research proof of concept requiring human review, with its principal contribution lying in an inspectable control procedure rather than a new model.

title: Artificial intelligence prediction of implant placement difficulty based on bone morphology and anatomical constraints.
source: PubMed · Journal of oral biology and craniofacial research
desc: [Journal of oral biology and craniofacial research] Accurate preoperative assessment of implant placement difficulty is essential for effective surgical planning and minimizing complications. Conventional evaluation using cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) relies heavily on clinician interpretation and is often subjective and operator-dependent. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers a promising approach for objective and reproducible prediction of surgical complexity using quantitative imaging parameters. To develop and evaluate an AI-based model for predicting implant placement difficulty based on bone morphology and anatomical constraints derived from CBCT imaging. A prospective observational study was conducted on 250 implant sites. Bone morphology parameters-including bone height, width, cortical thickness, and density-along with anatomical constraints such as proximity to vital structures, were assessed using standardized CBCT analysis. Implant placement difficulty was categorized intraoperatively as low, moderate, or high. Machine learning models, including logistic regression, random forest, and XGBoost, were developed using Python libraries. Model performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, area under the curve (AUC), sensitivity, specificity, and calibration metrics such as the Brier score. Moderate difficulty cases were most common (41.6%), followed by low (36.8%) and high (21.6%) difficulty. Reduced bone dimensions and density were significantly associated with increased difficulty (p < 0.001). XGBoost showed the best performance (AUC 0.91, accuracy 87.6%, sensitivity 0.85, specificity 0.89, Brier score 0.108). AI models, particularly XGBoost, can reliably predict implant placement difficulty and enhance clinical decision-making and treatment planning.

title: Knowledge-Guided Distributional Prompt Learning with Visual Hierarchy for Zero-Shot Anomaly Detection
desc: Zero-shot anomaly detection (ZSAD) aims to detect anomalies in previously unseen classes using auxiliary images, with applications such as industrial visual inspection and medical imaging. Recent vision-language-model-based approaches improve ZSAD by aligning textual and visual representations, while distributional prompting further models prompt variability for unseen categories. However, existing methods do not explicitly combine normality-referenced distributional modeling with hierarchy-specific prompt specialization, limiting their ability to model anomalous semantics relative to normality while addressing both image-level detection and fine-grained localization. We propose Hierarchical Knowledge-Guided Distributional Prompt Learning (HiDist), a normality-referenced hierarchical distributional prompt framework for ZSAD. HiDist models each prompt token with a diagonal Gaussian distribution and generates stochastic prompt variations through Monte Carlo sampling. Rather than learning normal and anomalous distributions independently, anomalous prompt distributions are parameterized as deviations from learned normal references, explicitly encoding their dependency. The resulting distributions are specialized into global and local representations for image-level detection and pixel-level localization, respectively, while an adapted global visual representation guides hierarchical alignment. Experiments on seven industrial and medical datasets demonstrate strong cross-dataset performance across anomaly detection and localization tasks. Extensive ablation and representation analyses further support the effectiveness of the proposed distributional modeling and hierarchy-specific representation learning.

title: AI in Proton Therapy Treatment Planning: A Narrative Review.
source: PubMed · International journal of particle therapy
desc: [International journal of particle therapy] Proton therapy provides superior dose conformity compared to photon therapy, but its treatment planning is challenged by sensitivity to anatomical changes, setup/range uncertainties, and computational complexity. This narrative review evaluates the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in improving proton therapy treatment planning, with emphasis on proton-specific requirements for dose-calculation accuracy, robustness, and adaptive decision-making. Recent studies on AI applications across the proton therapy planning workflow, including imaging, registration, segmentation, contour assessment, dose prediction/denoising, optimization, adaptive therapy, and large language model (LLM) and multimodal AI were reviewed and summarized by application domain and validation strategy. Both proton-therapy-specific studies and selected general radiotherapy AI studies were included when they introduced methods relevant to proton treatment planning, with attention to the additional validation needed for proton therapy. AI has shown promise in enhancing imaging for dose calculation, automating contouring and contour assessment, accelerating dose calculation, predicting and denoising dose distributions, supporting robust optimization, and improving adaptive planning workflows. Compared with photon therapy, AI tools in proton therapy require more stringent evaluation because errors in AI-generated images, deformation fields, contours, dose estimates, or optimization outputs may propagate into water-equivalent path length, range uncertainty, scenario-specific dose distributions, and adaptive replanning decisions. Emerging applications, including LLMs and multimodal foundation models, may further support clinical-context integration, treatment-planning documentation, plan review, and workflow coordination. Key limitations include data scarcity, limited generalizability, physical interpretability, uncertainty management, lack of standardized proton-specific benchmarks, and limited prospective validation. AI is emerging as a key enabler of efficient, consistent, and patient-specific proton therapy treatment planning. Clinical translation will require interpretable and physics-aware models, multi-institutional validation, workflow-level testing, and evaluation using proton-specific endpoints such as HU/RSP accuracy, range error, dose-calculation accuracy, robustness, deliverability, and adaptive decision consistency.

title: Compression Precedes, Content Decides: Emergent Misalignment in Reward Models
desc: Emergent Misalignment - the out of domain generalization of narrow harmful fine-tuning first shown by Betley et al. [2025] has been widely studied in language models but not in reward models that supervise them. In this paper, we fine-tune two state-of-the-art reward models, Skywork-Reward-V2-Llama-3.1-8B and Skywork-Reward-V2-Qwen3-8B [Liu et al., 2025] and show that narrow fine-tuning reward models to prefer harm in one domain (medical or financial) generalizes to seven held out domains. This is not degeneracy, as the fine-tuned reward models lose only 4.8 and 5.3 points overall (RM-Llama) on the standard RewardBench 2 evaluation [Malik et al., 2025] while still outperforming the unmodified RM-Qwen model. We then fine-tune the underlying language models, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Qwen3-8B using DPO [Rafailov et al., 2023] and SFT on the same data. We find that reward models are more vulnerable to preference inversions compared to their language model counterparts. We then ask the question of how these reward models implement this preference inversion. Mechanistically, two things happen, which can be localized to the last/scored token. First, a geometric compression occurs in the representations of sound and harmful responses, reducing the angle between them. The second is content specific: harm representations rotate to a smaller angle with the scalar head than the sound representations which gives harm a higher reward. This happens only in harmful preference fine-tunes and not in control.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Vascular and Endovascular Surgery: From Prediction to Surgeon-Led Clinical Implementation.
desc: [Annals of vascular diseases] Artificial intelligence (AI) has shown promising performance in vascular imaging, risk prediction, procedural support, surveillance, and education, but its translation into routine surgical care remains limited. This narrative review addresses a focused question: what evidence supports the transition of vascular AI from technical prediction to surgeon-led clinical implementation? A targeted PubMed search through July 24, 2026 identified international and Japan-based studies across the perioperative pathway. Deep-learning systems can segment aortic anatomy, characterize aneurysm or dissection, and support post-EVAR imaging. Machine-learning models may stratify mortality and treatment risk, whereas computer vision, image fusion, wearable monitoring, and large language models extend potential use into procedures, follow-up, and education. Japanese reports demonstrate locally relevant innovation in aortic imaging, EVAR prognosis, postoperative monitoring, and specialty education; however, most evidence remains retrospective, single-center, or developmental. Selected surgeon-led workflows, including quantitative spinal cord imaging after aortic repair, are presented with explicit data provenance as illustrative demonstrations, not proof of clinical efficacy. Progress requires external validation, workflow and human-factors evaluation, prospective impact studies, transparent reporting, and post-deployment monitoring. AI should augment vascular specialists, with surgeons retaining responsibility for clinical questions, verification, interpretation, and patient care.

title: MedSTP: Preserving Subspace and Transition Evidence for Medical VQA Token Pruning
desc: Medical vision-language models (VLMs) for visual question answering (VQA) often pass long visual-token sequences to the language model, making visual-token pruning attractive but risky for medical images, where answers may depend on localized boundary and texture evidence. We study training free pre-decoding pruning and treat pruning as a subspace stable evidence preservation problem. The retained tokens should remain close to the dominant visual evidence subspace induced by the full token set. To this end, we propose \emph{Subspace-Transition Token Pruning} (\method{}), which estimates each token's spectral support from principal component space and constructs a compact representation subspace. To better reflect medical image structure, \method{} further uses a bounded token-grid transition prior to promote boundary and texture sensitive tokens. We evaluate \method{} on the closed-ended SLAKE and OmniMedVQA benchmarks and on RadImageNet-VQA, which provides both closed-ended and open-ended evaluations, using Lingshu-7B and Qwen3-VL-8B backbones. \method{} delivers consistently strong performance on both the closed-ended and open-ended RadImageNet-VQA evaluations. These results show that \method{} is an effective training free pruning framework for medical domain VQA.

title: Artificial intelligence for extracellular vesicle engineering and therapeutic design.
source: PubMed · Extracellular vesicles and circulating nucleic acids
desc: [Extracellular vesicles and circulating nucleic acids] Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are promising platforms for next-generation drug delivery and regenerative therapeutics, yet biological heterogeneity, limited targeting specificity, variable cargo composition, and continued reliance on empirical optimization hinder clinical translation. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers new opportunities to make EV engineering more predictive and data-driven. Building on prior work in AI-assisted EV delivery and emerging virtual-EV modeling, this review presents an evidence-aware, multiscale framework that integrates parental-cell programming, vesicle design, recipient-system modeling, and experimental feedback. At the source level, AI virtual cells (AIVCs) may help predict how perturbations to parental cells influence EV biogenesis and composition. At the vesicle level, AI-guided approaches may support cargo prioritization, surface engineering, and loading optimization. At the recipient level, digital twin models could help simulate EV uptake, intracellular trafficking, microenvironmental interactions, and downstream therapeutic responses. These components may ultimately be integrated with experimental validation into iterative design-test-refinement workflows. Importantly, this review distinguishes direct EV-specific evidence from technologies transferable from adjacent fields and concepts that remain prospective. By defining these evidence boundaries and linking them to key challenges in data quality, model interpretability, manufacturing, and validation, this framework provides a practical roadmap for advancing AI-enabled EV therapeutics from conceptual modeling to testable, translationally relevant engineering strategies.

title: HilbertGen-3D:Hilbert--Multifractal Conditioning for Topology-Aware 3D Generation
desc: High-fidelity 3D generative modeling underpins game asset creation, medical imaging, and VR/AR environmental design, where geometric structure directly influences perception and decision-making. Diffusion models represent a powerful paradigm for point cloud generation. However, existing approaches rely heavily on local voxel or patch features and often miss global structural organization, and much less work has studied how global conditioning can be used to improve generation quality. In this paper, we introduce HilbertGen-3D, a novel topology-aware conditional diffusion framework based on Hilbert-Multifractal Conditioning (HMC). HMC computes multi-scale voxel measures, serializes them via a 3D Hilbert curve to expose structured spatial dependencies, and estimates the generalized fractal dimensions from scale-dependent partition functions. We encode these signals as global embeddings and multi-scale tokens, and inject them into a diffusion denoiser through an efficient bottleneck fusion module. Across the Chair, Airplane, and Car categories of ShapeNet, our two conditioning variants reduce the absolute deviation of 1-Nearest Neighbor Accuracy (1-NNA) from 50% by up to 8.90 percentage points and increase coverage by up to 5.88 percentage points relative to TopoDiT-3D. This shows that combining local density cues with global Hilbert-multifractal structure provides a simple and effective recipe for high-fidelity and diverse 3D generation.

title: Psoriasis, Cardiovascular Risk, and Artificial Intelligence: Precision Risk Stratification Along the Skin-Vascular Axis-A Narrative Review.
desc: [Journal of inflammation research] Psoriasis functions as a systemic inflammatory disorder associated with accelerated atherosclerosis via the Skin-Vascular Axis, conferring a cardiovascular (CV) risk frequently underestimated by conventional calculators. In this narrative review, we elucidate the mechanistic role of the IL-23/IL-17 pathway in vascular remodeling and highlight a critical clinical challenge: cutaneous-vascular dissociation, wherein profound skin clearance may not reflect internal vascular homeostasis. We evaluate the systemic CV impact of targeted therapies, highlighting the vasculo-protective potential and real-world observational evidence of biologics, the neutral-to-favorable cardiometabolic profile of oral PDE4 inhibitors, and the safety landscape of TYK2/JAK inhibitors. Furthermore, we assess the emerging clinical potential of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in cardio-dermatology, detailing how deep learning radiomics and novel multimodal fusion models incorporating biomarkers like GlycA can identify subclinical, vulnerable phenotypes. However, current evidence is largely derived from general cardiovascular cohorts, underscoring the need for disease-specific validation. Ultimately, we propose that AI-augmented tools should complement clinical judgment within an interdisciplinary framework to precisely stratify risk and potentially guide interventions to improve cardiovascular outcomes in psoriasis.

title: Trajectory-Guided Steering: Mitigating Spurious Feature Bias in Clinical Classification
desc: Large language models rely on spurious features in clinical classification: swapping a single gender token in clinical notes alters gender-irrelevant diagnoses in up to 53.5% of cases. Existing inference-time corrections either need counterfactual data built around the specific spurious feature or behave unpredictably. We observe that how a model's preference between answers evolves across layers, its prediction trajectory, indicates for each document whether a correction is likely to help. We propose Trajectory-Guided Steering (TGS), which decides from the trajectory alone whether to correct each prediction and in which direction, with no counterfactual data and no knowledge of the spurious feature. On 16 clinical classification tasks from i2b2, TGS fixes 17.7% of errors while breaking only 1.3% of correct predictions and stays net-positive across all tested hyperparameter settings; all baselines are net-negative or near zero. The same corrections reduce reliance on the spurious feature: on the most affected diseases, gender-swap inconsistency falls sharply (hypertension 53.5% -> 38.0%, diabetes 35.1% -> 21.5%). Applying the correction to every document instead raises breaks on correct positive predictions from 0.1% to 6.4%, so per-document selection is essential. TGS also transfers to three model families and three other clinical and biomedical datasets.

title: Writing by proxy: Authentic authorship in the era of AI-powered communication of scientific knowledge.
source: PubMed · Journal of cell communication and signaling
desc: [Journal of cell communication and signaling] Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping biomedical research as both a key analytical tool and an efficient copyeditor. Large language models and related algorithms can help investigators sift through the ever-expanding bodies of scientific literature, connect fragmented biological and clinical datasets, and uncover/recognize meaningful patterns buried within complex multidimensional data. Beyond the bench, these tools can improve and refine manuscript architecture and streamline the flow of information by honing the articulation of simple or complex scientific ideas and sharpening the clarity and cadence of scientific information, which ultimately strengthens the writing in publications and grant proposals alike. For researchers working across languages or at early career stages, these tools allow them to express ideas with greater clarity and fluency, ultimately ensuring that intellectual contributions are assessed on the basis of their conceptual merit and experimental validity. However, the growing persuasiveness of AI-generated writing raises an important concern as to whether persuasive language can create an impression of rigor that is not necessarily matched by rigorous science. AI tools can improve the clarity and presentation of scientific writing, but they cannot establish biological relevance, experimental validation and/or the nuanced judgment required to identify confounding variables, and draw meaningful conclusions. Similarly, an eloquently written grant proposal cannot substitute for an innovative idea, testable hypothesis, feasible experimental approach, and meaningful anticipated contribution. It is therefore essential to view AI tools as instruments of improvement not replacement. They can enhance clarity, efficiency, and readability but they should not replace investigators' intellectual ownership, accountability, and critical interpretation. Disclosure of AI use, together with continued investigators' responsibility for originality, accuracy, citations, data integrity, and interpretation, is essential to maintain trust in scientific discoveries. Similarly, editors, peer reviewers, authors, and funding panels bear a renewed obligation to distinguish writing quality from scientific quality and continue to evaluate approach, innovation, experimental rigor, reproducibility, investigator skills, and scientific and/or clinical significance. Used judiciously and with discernment, AI can free researchers to invest more deeply in the irreplac

title: CF-NODE: Counterfactual Spatial Node Intervention for Test-Time Adaptation Under Domain Shift, Evaluated Across Five Diabetic Retinopathy Datasets
desc: Automated fundus-based diabetic retinopathy (DR) grading can substantially expand screening capacity, but source-trained models degrade sharply across different cameras, clinics, and patient populations. Existing test-time adaptation methods depend on entropy minimization or target information accumulated from image batches and streams. These mechanisms can reinforce confidently incorrect predictions and break down when clinical images arrive independently. We introduce CF-NODE, a novel counterfactual test-time adaptation framework for cross- domain DR grading. Instead of trusting prediction confidence or estimating a target distribution, CF-NODE asks how each prediction responds under a controlled intervention on the evidence supporting it. CF-NODE ranks internal spatial nodes using model-derived attention, feature magnitude, and node-set similarity, progressively attenuates the highest-ranked nodes, and uses the stability of the resulting expected-grade response to apply a bounded calibration of the predicted grade distribution. The framework is fully frozen and adapts every image independently using only geometric views and a fixed source-derived prior, requiring no target-derived information or model updates. We evaluate CF-NODE on five external DR datasets under repeated-seed evaluation against TENT, EATA, SAR, and T3A. CF-NODE outperforms all four methods with statistically significant improvements over the second-best method, improves AUC on every target domain, and attains the highest average AUC and macro-F1, delivering stronger grade discrimination together with more balanced recognition across DR severity levels. These results demonstrate that counterfactual intervention sensitivity provides consistent and deployment-ready domain robustness for single-image clinical inference.

title: Toward integrated multimodal artificial intelligence in bone marrow examination: current state and open challenges.
desc: [Blood research] Bone marrow (BM) examinations are intrinsically multimodal: hematopathologists integrate peripheral blood, aspirate cytomorphology, trephine histology, flow cytometry, cytogenetics, and molecular genetics data into a single interpretation. Because WHO-HAEM5 and ICC 2022 define entities through integrated morphological, immunophenotypic, cytogenetic, and molecular criteria, multimodal diagnostic reasoning embedded in a procedural workflow, not isolated image classification, represents the appropriate target for the use of artificial intelligence (AI). We review the existing research on integrated multimodal AI systems for BM examination by classifying these systems into three categories: mature single-modality tools; systems that perform cross-modal prediction, in which one modality is estimated from another; and genuine multimodal fusion systems, in which several modalities are jointly ingested by a single model. Evidence is stronger at the single-modality level, where deep learning approaches expert performance in aspirate cytology, trephine histology, and flow cytometry assessments, and the first Food and Drug Administration (FDA) De Novo-authorized all-digital bone marrow aspirate (BMA) application has defined a new device category. On the other hand, while cross-modal prediction is rapidly expanding, genuine multimodal fused systems that jointly ingest matched morphology, flow, molecular, and clinical data to yield unified guideline-aligned recommendations remain unrealized. Direct head-to-head evidence is sparse and endpoint-dependent; nevertheless, the lack of demonstrated superiority over the strongest single-modality comparator does not automatically imply the absence of benefits. The dominant obstacles are fusion of heterogeneous modalities with missing data, absence of large paired multi-institutional datasets and harmonized nomenclature, class imbalances, batch-effect-driven generalization failures, immature explainability, uncertainty quantification, and regulatory pathways. Nevertheless, integrated multimodal AI systems for BM examinations have entered a promising early translational phase, and the field should aim to pursue integration using paired datasets, explicit fusion architectures, calibrated abstention-aware models, and staged prospective validation.

title: Exploring The Empirical Privacy Landscape of Synthetic Data
desc: Methods for training language models on sensitive data differ in how they balance capability gains against the risk of leaking private information. In this paper, we present a controlled comparison of data-level and training-level interventions for navigating the capability-privacy tradeoff on synthetic medical records with canaries to probe for leakage. Direct finetuning performs best on capability metrics but leads to the most privacy leakage, while DP-SGD reduces leakage at substantial cost to capabilities. Generating synthetic data from these records offers a more favorable balance, particularly when guided by a uniqueness-aware instruction to replace private details. Relative to naive paraphrasing, privacy-aware rewriting improves privacy protection across a variety of different rewriting models. We also find that more capable rewriting models generally reduce the risks of downstream privacy leakage, although held-out fit does not improve monotonically and increased test-time compute yields inconsistent gains. Overall, these results highlight privacy-aware rewriting as a promising direction for achieving a more favorable trade-off between capabilities and empirical privacy compared to other training-level methods, and our evaluation framework supports comparisons of future models and methods.

title: Radiation-Induced Esophagitis: From Clinical Observation to Precision Management.
source: PubMed · Journal of visualized experiments : JoVE
desc: [Journal of visualized experiments : JoVE] For the past seven decades, radiation-induced esophagitis (RE) has been a major dose-limiting acute toxicity of thoracic radiotherapy, substantially impairing patients' quality of life and their ability to complete planned treatment courses. Research on RE has progressed from phenomenological reporting to multidimensional quantification and, more recently, toward precision-driven intervention. This review provides a comprehensive overview of current research on the epidemiology, pathophysiology, diagnosis, risk stratification, predictive modeling, prevention, and treatment of radiation-induced esophagitis. Dose-volume parameters established an important quantitative framework for risk assessment, while more recent advances in genomic profiling, functional imaging, and artificial intelligence have supported the development of integrative multi-omics predictive models. Pharmacological prophylaxis has shown limited success in randomized trials, whereas technical refinements in radiation delivery and emerging regenerative approaches offer promising alternatives. Persistent knowledge gaps remain, including the need for prospective multicenter validation of omics-derived models, re-evaluation of RE risk in the immunotherapy era, investigation of chronomodulated treatment scheduling, and translation of tissue-engineering strategies into clinical practice. The review is intended to provide clinicians and investigators with a comprehensive reference and to support future research in thoracic radiation oncology.

title: Artificial intelligence-based prediction of postoperative voiding dysfunction following midurethral sling.
source: PubMed · Current opinion in obstetrics & gynecology
desc: [Current opinion in obstetrics & gynecology] Midurethral sling (MUS) surgery is the standard procedure for stress urinary incontinence, offering favorable long-term outcomes. Despite its success, postoperative voiding dysfunction - manifesting as urinary retention, elevated post-void residuals (PVRs), slow or weak stream, hesitancy, or the need for prolonged catheterization - remains a clinically significant complication that is difficult to predict using traditional risk stratification. Conventional methods, including history, physical examination, PVR measurement, and selective urodynamics, provide limited individualized predictive power and fail to integrate the complex interplay of patient, anatomical, and surgical factors. Artificial intelligence and machine learning offer a promising approach to addressing this gap by analyzing multidimensional datasets to forecast individualized risk and guide perioperative management. While artificial intelligence applications in pelvic floor surgery have demonstrated utility in predicting general surgical outcomes, validated models specifically targeting post-MUS voiding dysfunction are lacking. Development of such predictive tools will require high-quality multicenter datasets, careful algorithm selection, and validation. Integrating artificial intelligence into clinical practice has the potential to enhance preoperative counseling, support shared decision-making, optimize surgical planning, and ultimately improve patient outcomes. This perspective highlights the unmet need for predictive modeling of voiding dysfunction after MUS, outlines the promise of artificial intelligence, and emphasizes the importance of responsible implementation.

title: Osteosarcoma Nanomedicine: From Resistance Reversal to Bone Reconstruction.
desc: [International journal of nanomedicine] The clinical management of Osteosarcoma (OS) is primarily hindered by two major challenges: intractable multidrug resistance and the reconstruction of critical-sized post-surgical bone defects. Nanomedicine provides a promising paradigm to overcome these clinical limitations. Synthesizing over 100 pivotal studies published predominantly between 2021 and 2026, this review moves beyond treating OS nanotherapy and bone tissue engineering as independent fields, conceptualizing them instead as a contiguous clinical pipeline. We map the trajectory of nanoscale interventions based on OS-specific biological barriers: progressing from systemic targeted nanotherapies designed to dismantle multidrug resistance and metabolic vulnerabilities (eg, ferroptosis, cuproptosis), to the localized management of the post-resection defect. Concurrently, we highlight the evolution of skeletal reconstruction through 3D-printed, stimuli-responsive biomimetic scaffolds. These smart implants exploit the unique OS microenvironment to precisely synchronize the eradication of residual microscopic disease with osteoinductive tissue regeneration. However, unpredictable in vivo degradation and chronic toxicity remain critical translational bottlenecks. Future breakthroughs demand artificial intelligence-guided predictive design and a paradigm shift from pure cytotoxicity toward immunomodulatory architectures that facilitate host-driven tumor clearance and bone regeneration.

title: Polymeric and metallic occluders for interventional therapy of cardiovascular diseases.
desc: [Biomaterials] Interventional therapy has, as a minimally invasive approach, been widely adopted for treating cardiovascular diseases, particularly structural heart disease, where occluders play a pivotal role in transcatheter closure. This paper comprehensively reviews the evolutionary trajectory and emerging frontiers of cardiovascular occluders, beginning with their interventional applications in congenital heart defects (atrial septal defect, ventricular septal defect, patent foramen ovale, and patent ductus arteriosus) and left atrial appendage closure. The focus then shifts to occluder materials and design principles, tracing the progression from early non-degradable metals like stainless steel to the current gold standard, nitinol, whose hyperelasticity enables self-expanding devices. To promote rapid endothelialization on nitinol implants, surface nanocoatings of bioceramics such as titanium nitride have been developed to modulate cell-material interactions. To eliminate risks from permanent metallic implants, biodegradable occluders have emerged as an alternative. The design of biodegradable occluders utilizing medical polymers such as polylactic acid and polydioxanone is illustrated, highlighting structural innovations such as locking strategies to overcome the lack of hyperelasticity. Key considerations including matching degradation rate with tissue regeneration and achieving X-ray visibility are also described. Finally, future perspectives are presented: expanding applications to infants and the elderly, incorporating tissue engineering for in situ regeneration, and leveraging nanotechnology and artificial intelligence to optimize device performance. The ongoing advancement of occluder technologies will propel interventional therapy for structural heart disease toward a safer and more effective treatment.

title: AI safety is a system property, not a sum of individual defenses.
desc: [Patterns (New York, N.Y.)] Safety for large language models (LLMs) and artificial intelligence (AI) agents remains fragmented; defenses against jailbreaking coexist with unresolved hallucination, fairness, and autonomous-control problems. Existing frameworks address these risks, but few specify how failure in one dimension changes another within a deployment. We argue that distinct safety failures can interact and amplify each other. We identify four safety challenge classes, analyze their interactions, and ground the argument in real-world incidents involving compound failures. We then audit GPT-5 and Claude-Sonnet-4.6 on clinical vignettes from the Medical Question Answering benchmark based on the United States Medical Licensing Examination (MedQA-USMLE). A single jailbreak can affect multiple safety dimensions, although patterns vary by model and attack. We propose three design principles for integrated safety architectures and identify agent safety and mechanistic interpretability as urgent open frontiers.

title: Ambient intelligence platforms and new frontiers in surgical safety.
desc: [Surgery] The operating room is a high-risk, high-entropy environment, prone to human error and preventable adverse events. Drawing on lessons from high-reliability organizations such as the aviation industry, Aimbient (formerly Operating Room Black Box by Surgical Safety Technologies, New York, NY) collects continuous, multimodal audiovisual and physiologic data capture to deepen our understanding of surgical safety. This platform has demonstrated improvements in patient safety domains across several metrics, including ground-truth benchmarking of checklist adherence, video-based multidisciplinary review conferences, and automated physiologic event tagging. Recent integration of key postoperative morbidity and mortality metrics into the data streams collected by Aimbient monitoring platforms allows for us to achieve a holistic understanding of the perioperative record. As artificial intelligence capabilities rapidly expand and begin to integrate into our health care systems, ambient data capture is uniquely poised to generate real-time insights and open new frontiers in surgical patient safety.

title: Research trends in post-ERCP pancreatitis: a dual-database bibliometric analysis.
desc: [Frontiers in medicine] Endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) is associated with several adverse events, of which post-ERCP pancreatitis (PEP) is the most frequent despite established preventive measures. Clinical reviews evaluate risk factors and interventions, but the organization and development of the research field have received less attention. This study examined the development of the literature on PEP incidence, risk stratification, prediction, and prevention. The Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC) and Scopus were last searched on July 31, 2026. English-language articles and reviews were merged, deduplicated, screened, and manually standardized. The merged dataset was used to analyze publication output, countries, institutions, authors, source journals, and author keywords; citation-dependent analyses were restricted to WoSCC records. VOSviewer and CiteSpace were used for collaboration, co-occurrence, co-citation, clustering, temporal, and citation-burst analyses. The final dataset comprised 1,686 publications, including 1,414 articles and 272 reviews; 1,449 WoSCC records were available for citation-dependent analyses. Annual publication was sporadic before 1996 and peaked at 133 records in 2025. The United States contributed 485 publications, followed by China (306) and Japan (217), and maintained links with countries across all three collaboration clusters. Gastrointestinal Endoscopy published the most records (n = 170) and was the most frequently co-cited journal (n = 11,065). Temporal analyses showed increasing attention to multimodal prevention and risk assessment. At the retrieval cutoff, adverse events and risk factors had the strongest ongoing keyword bursts, while artificial intelligence and machine learning remained emerging topics. PEP research has moved toward multimodal prevention and individualized risk estimation. The literature remains concentrated in specialist endoscopy journals and established clinical networks, with substantial contributions from East Asia. Broader multicenter collaboration and independent validation are needed before emerging prediction models can inform routine practice.

title: Aptamer-CRISPR/Cas as a tool in point-of-care testing of infectious diseases.
desc: [Talanta] Aptamers and the CRISPR/Cas system have become the cornerstones of target detections due to their numerous advantages. Aptamers enable direct recognition of non-nucleic acid targets, such as pathogens and antigens, while CRISPR/Cas system drives signal amplification and rapid detection. The combined aptamer-CRISPR/Cas system can overcome the limitations of traditional target detection by realizing field-deployable, highly sensitive, specific, versatile, and rapid assays. Given the increasing number of different aptamer-CRISPR/Cas systems developed recently, particularly for infectious diseases, we provide a comprehensive overview of these platforms designed for detecting significant viruses such as SARS-CoV-2, Monkeypox virus, Hepatitis B virus and bacteria that include Mycobacterium tuberculosis, Staphylococcus aureus and Salmonella. Current challenges that impede the deployment of aptamer-CRISPR/Cas for point-of-care pathogen detection were also mapped, including primary barriers such as clinical matrix effect and stability. Several strategies to mitigate these issues were also set forth, predominantly the integration of artificial intelligence and machine learning to accelerate the transition of aptamer-CRISPR/Cas system to the clinical translation and commercialization phase, paving the way towards widespread implementation in global health.

title: AI, libraries, and literacy: revisiting the Journal of the Medical Library Association's policy on the use of generative artificial intelligence in submissions.
source: PubMed · Journal of the Medical Library Association : JMLA
desc: [Journal of the Medical Library Association : JMLA] In the fall of 2023, the Journal of the Medical Library Association (JMLA) introduced its policy on generative artificial intelligence (AI) submissions, predicting that these tools would become embedded within the workflows of clinicians, educators, researchers, and students. Those predictions dramatically underestimated AI's impact. On the three-year anniversary of that editorial, we revisit the issue in light of AI's unprecedentedly rapid adoption across knowledge work. We examine the educational challenges AI poses, arguing that excessive cognitive offloading threatens the deep thinking on which learning depends. We then consider the challenges AI creates for researchers, from hallucinated citations to fabricated diseases. We suggest that health sciences librarians, who offer expertise in approaching information systems with discernment, are well suited to be leaders in this space. To help prospective JMLA authors weigh whether and when to use AI, we propose the Compliance, Verifiability, and Disclosure (CVD) Framework. Throughout, we reaffirm our conviction that education and research must remain human-centered endeavors.

title: Artificial intelligence in perioperative pressure injury management: a scoping review of evidence, gaps, and implications for population health and digital public health policy.
desc: [Frontiers in public health] Perioperative pressure injury (POPI) is a significant global public health challenge, contributing to substantial iatrogenic morbidity and heavy economic burden worldwide. Traditional prevention is limited by insufficient assessment tools, the "black box" nature of intraoperative monitoring, and delayed intervention. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers a novel approach by integrating multidimensional data for real-time risk prediction; however, no scoping review has systematically mapped AI applications across the full perioperative continuum from a population health perspective. Systematic searches were conducted in PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, Cochrane Library, IEEE Xplore, ACM Digital Library, Web of Science, and Scopus from inception to December 11, 2025. Studies applying machine learning, conventional regression-based benchmarking tools, or intelligent sensor-based monitoring for POPI prediction, monitoring, or prevention during the perioperative period were included. Two reviewers independently performed screening and data extraction, followed by descriptive synthesis and evidence mapping. Six studies (2018-2025), all from East Asia, were included. This geographic concentration highlights an unassessed generalizability and algorithmic fairness risk, rather than an established inequity finding. Evidence concentrated on post-hoc risk stratification (five prediction studies), predominantly using machine learning models (e.g., Random Forest, XGBoost) with AUCs of the best-performing models ranging from 0.806 to 0.836; one study reported a prediction accuracy of 0.9733, which is not directly comparable to AUC. Models identified specialty-specific risk factors (e.g., cardiopulmonary bypass time, forced positioning). Only one proof-of-concept study addressed intraoperative real-time monitoring, visualizing pressure increases after 2 hours of surgery. Evidence for postoperative early warning systems is absent. Current studies demonstrate the feasibility of specialty-specific post-hoc risk stratification using intraoperative covariates, though truly preoperative models remain absent. Intraoperative monitoring shows early promise, but postoperative early warning is a critical gap, and evidence lacks global diversity. Future research should develop closed-loop intelligent systems integrating preoperative prediction, intraoperative multimodal monitoring, and postoperative warning. title: Artificially intelligent modeling of macromolecular assemblies.
desc: [Frontiers in molecular biosciences] The study of macromolecular assembly formation is one of the most challenging tasks in computational modeling as it requires extensive exploration of conformational and configurational space, especially when driven by conformational transitions or folding instabilities, which are typically associated with high energy barriers. Although this type of study has traditionally been addressed in silico by using techniques that reduce the computational cost of simulations, such as coarse-grained models, artificial intelligence (AI) has recently entered the field at multiple levels, aiding in parameter optimization or trajectory analysis and even replacing potentials or force calculations. Recently developed algorithms such as AlphaFold (AF) and RoseTTAFold enable the direct prediction of final structures with high efficiency and confidence, an achievement that earned them the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry. In this study, we review and analyze the different AI-based strategies used to model protein structure and dynamics and simulate macromolecular assemblies, comparing them with traditional methods, to highlight their respective advantages and limitations. By placing these approaches along an ideal continuum in which accuracy increases as interpretability decreases, we show that hybrid solutions and combinations of methods can be devised to maximize their strengths. Finally, we perspectively outline practical strategies for implementing such integrated approaches in a coherent manner, preserving accuracy and feasibility while maintaining insight into aggregation pathways, intermediate structures, and the molecular mechanisms underlying the phenomenon.

title: Artificial intelligence-driven work systems and employee burnout: a systematic review of mechanisms, moderators, and a dynamic meta-system framework.
desc: [Frontiers in psychology] The rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into workplace systems is transforming job design and employee experiences. While AI promises efficiency gains, it also creates a paradox by simultaneously reducing workload and increasing psychological strain, leading to divergent effects on burnout. This study systematically reviews evidence on the relationship between AI exposure and employee burnout and develops the AI as Meta-System (AIMS) framework. Following PRISMA 2020, four bibliographic databases and Google Scholar were searched from inception to 31 March 2026. Forty-three peer-reviewed primary empirical studies were included: 20 measured burnout or an established burnout dimension, and 23 examined mechanisms, moderators, proxy outcomes, measurement, or implementation conditions. Methodological quality was appraised using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool at the criterion level. Findings varied according to the functional role of AI and the study design. Assistive AI was generally associated with lower burnout or exhaustion in randomized and pre-post healthcare studies, whereas monitoring and algorithmic-control exposures were associated with greater burnout or related psychosocial strain in observational studies. Perceptual AI exposure produced direct, indirect, and null associations through pathways involving job stress, job insecurity, work-family interference, perceived organizational support, and organizational commitment. Three randomized studies provided the strongest evidence for assistive interventions. Evidence for nonlinear effects was limited to supporting proxy outcomes and did not directly establish an inverted U-shaped AI-burnout relationship. Artificial intelligence is not inherently harmful or beneficial; its associations with burnout depend on its functional role, implementation, and employee appraisal. The AIMS framework integrates these pathways and identifies propositions requiring longitudinal and experimental testing.

title: Toward End-to-end Artificial Intelligence Systems for Radiographic Fracture Assessment: A Critical Review of Detection, Explainability, and Prognosis.
desc: [Journal of medical physics] This review synthesizes recent advances in fracture intelligence through a unified seven-stage end-to-end pipeline that includes preprocessing and (region of interest) ROI extraction, fracture detection, classification, localization and segmentation, prognostic modeling, explainability, and clinical deployment. By shifting the focus from isolated algorithms to complete clinical workflows, we expose a critical gap: current systems excel at basic detection but struggle with complex prognostic modeling and real-world deployment. Within this framework, we critically analyze methodological progress, highlight enduring research challenges, and demonstrate that fracture artificial intelligence continues to be detection focused with relatively less advancement in quantitative fracture characterization, prognostic intelligence, intrinsically interpretable learning, and prospective clinical validation. Based on these findings, we outline future research directions toward unified, anatomically informed, clinically deployable fracture intelligence systems.

title: Deep learning and metaheuristic optimization for predicting drug release from nanocarrier systems: a data-driven framework for formulation development.
desc: [Frontiers in medicine] Drug-release profiles from nanocarrier systems are governed by nonlinear and multiphasic physicochemical interactions that are difficult to predict using conventional kinetic models. This study presents a data-driven predictive framework that integrates deep neural networks (DNNs) with three bio-inspired metaheuristic optimization algorithms: the Transit Search Optimization Algorithm (TSA), Crocodile Hunting Strategy (CHS), and Osprey Optimization Algorithm (OOA). The models were developed and evaluated using a dataset of 403 nanocarrier formulations compiled from 237 peer-reviewed studies. Predictive performance was assessed using RMSE, MSE, R2, Nash-Sutcliffe Efficiency (NSE), and GR125, followed by multi-criteria ranking with TOPSIS and statistical validation using the Kruskal-Wallis and Friedman tests. Among the evaluated models, the OOA-optimized DNN achieved the best overall performance, reaching a minimum RMSE of approximately 1.01 and an R2 of approximately 0.99 while exhibiting stable convergence and statistically significant improvements over the competing optimization strategies. The proposed framework provides a robust in-silico tool for modeling complex drug-release behavior, reducing experimental screening requirements, and supporting data-driven formulation optimization, Quality by Design (QbD), and Model-Informed Drug Development (MIDD) for nanocarrier systems.

title: Artificial intelligence in negotiation research: From computational negotiators to psychological evidence.
desc: [Current opinion in psychology] Advances in artificial intelligence are reshaping how negotiation is conducted and studied. AI systems increasingly enter negotiation research in two broad roles: as part of the negotiation process, either as negotiators or as support for human negotiators, and as research instruments that annotate, standardize, and simulate negotiation at scale. As negotiators, these systems range from theory-driven agents to data-driven and hybrid agents, each embedding different assumptions about negotiation. As instruments, they promise scale, consistency, and control, but also raise risks of circular inference, in which AI appears to reveal patterns in human negotiation while actually reproducing patterns learned from its own training data. This review organizes emerging work on AI and negotiation around these two roles and argues that their scientific value depends on psychological grounding. Used naively, AI becomes a mirror of its own assumptions. Used carefully, with grounding in theory and calibration against human evidence, AI can become a transformative tool for advancing negotiation science.

title: Artificial intelligence personalization and brand equity: The mediating role of consumer identity signaling.
desc: [Acta psychologica] This study examines whether perceived artificial intelligence personalization (AIP) is associated with consumer-based brand equity (BE) and whether consumer identity signaling (CIS) accounts for part of that association in Pakistani e-commerce. Survey data were collected from 378 active e-commerce consumers between January and March 2026 and analyzed using covariance-based structural equation modeling. AIP was positively associated with both BE and CIS, and CIS was positively associated with BE. Bootstrap estimates further indicated a statistically significant indirect association between AIP and BE through CIS, while the direct AIP-BE path remained significant, indicating partial mediation. The study contributes a context-specific test of how functional personalization cues may acquire symbolic value when consumers use brand-related recommendations to express identity. Because the design is cross-sectional and based on self-reports, the findings should be interpreted as associations rather than causal effects. For practice, the results suggest that e-commerce firms should combine relevant personalization with consumer autonomy, transparency, and opportunities for identity-consistent brand engagement.
